name: Free-convex-domain Heilbronn problem for 12 points
definition: Choose 12 distinct rational points in the plane, with no three collinear. Maximize the minimum area of a triangle formed by three chosen points divided by the area of their convex hull. There are no coordinate bounds and no fixed outer container.
solution_format: An object with points, a list of 12 [x,y] coordinate pairs. Coordinates may be integers, rational strings such as '3/2', or finite decimal numbers interpreted by their decimal representation.
constraints: Coordinates are rational numbers with no magnitude bound.
No three points are collinear, so the minimum triangle area is positive.
The denominator is the area of the convex hull of the 12 points; the hull has positive area.
There is no fixed square, triangle, or other container.

parameters.coordinate_domain: unbounded rational coordinates in the plane
parameters.container: convex hull of the selected points

verification: The checker parses exact rational coordinates, rejects duplicates and every collinear triple, enumerates all 220 triangle areas, computes the convex hull with an exact monotone-chain algorithm, and returns the exact ratio of the minimum triangle area to hull area.

source_review.definition: Twelve points in a free convex planar domain; maximize minimum triangle area divided by convex hull area. This functional differs from fixed-square T005. No rational-coordinate magnitude cap; rational approximation preserves the continuous supremum by continuity on general-position configurations.
source_review.primary_record: Current Tejstead free-convex n12 archive gives 2/51, credited to David Cantrell June2007; source notes original Mathematica notebook received September2026. Local baseline independently rebuilds archived decimals by affine normalization and rational reconstruction; does not assert byte identity with the original notebook.
source_review.independent_reproduction: Root independently normalized source and recovered exact half-integer coordinates. Enumerated 220 triangles, minimum doubled area 1/2. A separate directed-support-edge enumeration, without formal Andrew hull algorithm, gives nine hull edges and doubled hull area 51/4; exact ratio2/51.

No claim that a finite numerical check establishes mathematical optimality.
